Describe the concrete problem, intended behavior and current evidence. For a defect,
give the version, a minimal reproduction and the expected and observed behavior.

- Scope: bounded component, integrated continuing behavior, or infrastructure.
  Name the goal epic it serves, [the Doom player #118](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/issues/118) or
  [language #173](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/issues/173), or the milestone issue it extends; behavior over
  time follows the [principle](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/main/AGENTS.md#coherent-behavior-over-time).
- Boundary: name the implemented model, live and held state, information supplied
  by adapters, and any proposed change within the same coupled global equilibrium.
- Evidence: give the simpler control, acceptance and preservation gates, failures,
  and remaining limits. Infrastructure can explain applicability without an
  unrelated whole-brain acceptance test.

For sequence claims, identify the continuing learned context and temporal
organization. Test retained, absent and perturbed context with matched exposure,
plus recovery or counterfactual contexts where relevant. Sequential output,
sensory feedback, trace, memory and efference are permitted; next-event accuracy
or self-feeding alone is bounded component evidence. Separate numerical residual
from musical surprise and sequence quality. Default `Brain.act` with held trace
is not a joint future-trajectory solve. No new phrase module or whole-song-at-once
output is required; adapters must not hide answers, phase or arrangement.

See the [scope and preservation review](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#scope-and-evidence-for-behavior-over-time).
